body: Byju's (Think & Learn) was valued at ~$22 bn in 2022, up from ~$5 bn in 2020, after a debt-and-equity-funded acquisition spree (Aakash ~$950 m, WhiteHat Jr ~$300 m, Great Learning, Epic, Toppr). FY21 accounts were filed ~18 months late with a restated loss of ~Rs 4,588 cr after auditor Deloitte forced deferral of upfront revenue recognition; FY22 loss ~Rs 8,245 cr. In Jun 2023 Deloitte resigned (citing delayed statements) and three board members (Prosus, Peak XV/Sequoia, Chan-Zuckerberg) quit. Lenders of a $1.2 bn term loan alleged default and that ~$533 m was moved to a small Miami hedge fund. BlackRock and Prosus cut marks to $11 bn, $5 bn and eventually near zero. Insolvency was admitted in Jul 2024 over BCCI dues; successor auditor BDO resigned in Sep 2024. Visible flags: (1) revenue recognised upfront on EMI-financed courses; (2) aggressive sales practices and refund complaints; (3) late filings and auditor change; (4) founder-controlled board with investors lacking information; (5) leverage via covenant-lite US loan to buy growth. Lesson for IPO-bound/private names: delayed audited accounts, auditor resignations and board exits are disqualifiers regardless of brand; check revenue recognition and CFO vs reported growth.

data.early_signals: upfront revenue recognition; 18-month delayed accounts; Deloitte exit; board resignations; TLB covenant disputes
data.lesson: Late accounts + auditor exit = walk away
data.spotted_by: auditor Deloitte; US lenders; journalists (The Ken, Morning Context)

title: Byju's: $22 bn edtech to insolvency (2022-2024, private)
